name: Basic_Model (ideal PZT, buffer and ADC)
description: One PZT (SM311) -> ideal unity buffer with a bias resistor -> ideal ADC. No parasitics, no MUX, all components ideal; the only capacitance is the PZT. The bias resistor goes to ground (default, ADC range -VDD/2 .. +VDD/2) or to VMID (0 .. VDD); the ADC resolution and sampling rate are adjustable.

components.group: PZT sensor (SM311 / PZT-5H class, ideal: charge source || Cp)

items.label: Capacitance (override)
items.tip: empty = calculated from size, thickness and eps33. A value replaces the calculated sensor capacitance Cp.

items.label: Force gain
items.tip: Scales the applied force (sensitivity scatter, force coupling).

items.label: Supply VDD
items.tip: System rail (3.3 V). An ideal buffer has no rails; VDD only sets the ADC range: -VDD/2 .. +VDD/2 with the bias on ground, 0 .. VDD with the bias on VMID.

items.label: Bias resistor goes to
items.tip: ground (default): the sensor node rests at 0 V and swings both ways, the ADC range is -VDD/2 .. +VDD/2 (-1.65 .. +1.65 V). vmid: the node rests at the VMID level and the ADC range is 0 .. VDD (0 .. 3.3 V).

items.label: VMID reference
items.tip: Level of the VMID source (used when the bias goes to VMID).

items.label: Bias resistor
items.tip: From the sensor node / buffer input to ground or VMID. With Cp it sets the decay time constant of the signal.

items.label: Initial sensor node voltage
items.tip: Start condition of the sensor node. Empty = the bias level (0 V on ground, VMID otherwise).

items.label: Resolution (ADC-Out)
items.tip: Bits of the derived ADC-Out value (default 12). LSB = (range span) / 2^bits; the span is VDD in both bias modes.

items.label: ADC sampling rate
items.tip: The buffer output is sampled instantly every 1/rate. Type 50k for 50 kHz. The number of conversions is run duration x rate.

items.label: First sample at
items.tip: Time of the first conversion; the next ones follow every sampling period.

items.label: Run duration
items.tip: Length of the simulated time. Make it long enough for the force profile and for several conversions at the chosen rate.

items.label: Maximum time step
items.tip: Empty = automatic: 1/20 of the sampling period and 1/1000 of the run. The conversion instants and the force corners are solver breakpoints, so a coarser step stays accurate.

items.label: Relative tolerance
items.tip: QSPICE solver tolerance. The QSPICE default 1e-3 leaves ~0.5 mV of error on a 0.5 V signal; 1e-6 brings it below 0.1 mV (below an LSB up to about 14 bit). Raise it for very long runs.

items.label: White noise (RMS)
items.tip: RMS (standard deviation) of independent Gaussian white noise added to the ADC input value at every conversion, before quantisation: v_out = quant(v_in + N(0, sigma)). It is applied at the conversion instants, so it needs no new simulation. 0 = off.

items.label: Noise seed
items.tip: Seed of the noise generator: the same seed gives the same noise, so runs stay repeatable and comparable against a held reference.

tables.title: Input profile: force pulses
tables.tip: One row per trapezoidal force pulse on the sensor (address 0). Rows add up. With the bias on ground the swing limit is about 0.17 N for a 0.7 mm sensor (open circuit, before the bias resistor drains it).

tables.title: Input profile: sine waves
tables.tip: One row per sinusoidal force on the sensor (address 0): F = amplitude x sin(2 pi f t) for the given number of cycles starting at Start (zero before and after). Rows add up and also add to the pulses above.
